Which world stays geologically active the longest?
the largest one, because it keeps its internal heat
the closest to the Sun, because sunlight heats its core
the one with the most craters
the smallest one, because it cools evenly

slides.reveal: Answer: A. Volcanism and tectonics run on internal heat, and large worlds keep their heat longest because they have less surface per unit of volume to lose it through.

Why does the Moon have far more craters than Earth?
Earth erased its craters with erosion, lava and plates
the Moon is a bigger target than Earth
Earth's air stops every incoming rock
impacts began only after Earth had formed

slides.reveal: Answer: A. Earth was hit at least as often as the Moon (it is a bigger target with stronger gravity), but on Earth erosion by water and wind, volcanic lava and plate tectonics have erased or buried almost all old craters.

Venus and Earth are almost the same size. Why is Venus 464 °C?
air traps heat: a runaway greenhouse
it is closer to the Sun than Mercury is
its core is much hotter than Earth's core
its volcanoes are erupting everywhere today

slides.reveal: Answer: A. Venus's 92-bar, 96.5% carbon dioxide atmosphere traps infrared heat; the runaway greenhouse boiled away its water, and without oceans the carbon dioxide stayed in the air (slide 13).
